chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who performed the morning prayer at night, being misled in that by the moon, then slept until the sun rose, and was then informed that he had prayed at night, he عليه السلام said: “He repeats his prayer.”

key_terms.الْغَدَاةَ: the morning prayer, meaning Fajr salat
key_terms.الْقَمَرُ: the moon, whose light led to the mistaken assumption of dawn
key_terms.بِلَيْلٍ: at night, before the valid time of the prayer had begun
key_terms.طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun rose, indicating the passage of the prayer time
key_terms.غَرَّهُ: misled him or caused him to be deceived

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prays Fajr at night by mistake, thinking dawn has entered?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who performs salat al-ghadah before its proper time due to mistaking moonlight for dawn. Since the prayer was offered at night and not within its valid time, it must be repeated.
